source.title: Difference in Euclidean Norm Can Cause Semantic Divergence in Batch Normalization
source.authors: Zhen-Nan Wang; Ke-Han Li; Runyi Yu; Yian Zhao; Peng-Chong Qiao; Chang Liu; Fan Xu; Xiang Ji; Guoli Song; Jie Chen

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares L2 BN with BN and reports classification results and training curves, but it does not test whether training reaches zero or near-zero training classification error, or whether BN speeds training versus no normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy and says L2 BN has slightly smaller training loss than BN for the plotted models. It does not report training classification error. Results about the L2 BN versus BN comparison do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: Section 3.1 relies on BN's established optimization benefit while evaluating an added L2 normalization step. Its own results compare normalization methods for test accuracy, feature geometry and training loss; they do not test any listed version. In particular, V6 requires a BN-versus-no-BN training-speed or learning-rate-tolerance comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that L2 BN improves classification performance and feature discriminability across image and acoustic classification experiments without extra parameters or hyperparameters. Intra-class compactness does not improve for every backbone, although the combined intra/inter-angle ratio improves for all tested CIFAR100 backbones.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds per-sample L2 normalization before batch normalization and compares this variant with BN; it does not evaluate the original claim's training-error outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.1 and Figure 6 describe slightly smaller training loss for L2 BN than BN for ResNet-56 on CIFAR100 and ResNet-50 on ImageNet-1K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding per-sample L2 normalization before BN can slightly reduce training loss relative to BN in these settings.

record.problems: The training-loss comparison is described qualitatively and shown as a curve without reported numeric values. The study does not measure training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No other result rows retained: the paper's classification accuracy results are test accuracy, and its other reported metrics concern feature angles and inter/intra-class ratios rather than the claim's training-error outcomes.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth in plain networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, including recovery and divergence.
BN's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance versus the same network without BN, and Fixup's normalization-free alternative.

record.verdict_notes: Test accuracy and feature-angle results are already declared in rows_left_out and do not measure the listed optimization claims. No verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error, corrupted or random labels, or the listed model-size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or spurious-minimum outcome.
Does not compare plain and residual networks for training error as depth changes.
Does not compare initializations or measure trainable depth.
Does not study learning rates relative to stability limits or sharpness.
Compares L2 BN with BN, not BN with the same network without batch normalization; it does not test BN's effect on learning speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: ResNet-56
rows.operation_detail: Compared BN and L2 BN models under the same configurations; plotted training loss.
rows.value: L2 BN: slightly smaller training loss
rows.note: The text characterizes the difference as slight; no numeric training-loss values are reported.
rows.check: The subject, baseline and qualitative value match Section 4.1 and Figure 6(a), but this is the study's own method compared with BN and should not be retained as a claim-result row. Slightly lower training loss establishes neither near-zero training classification error (V1) nor BN's speed advantage over an unnormalized network (V6); 'partial' is therefore inappropriate.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
